name: @qase/mcp-server

tools.name: qase_api
tools.description: Call any Qase REST endpoint directly, for the few things no dedicated tool covers: method, a /v1/… path on the configured host, optional body or query. Prefer a dedicated tool where one exists — they normalize enums and validate before spending a call. JSON only; uploads go through qase_attachment_upload. A DELETE asks for confirmation like the dedicated delete tools. Cost: one API call, 0.3-1.5s.

path.description: API path starting with a version segment (e.g., "/v1/project/DEMO/run")

tools.name: qase_attachment_delete
tools.description: Delete an attachment by its hash (from qase_attachment_upload). Anything referencing it keeps the reference but the file is gone; this cannot be undone. Asks the user for confirmation first. Cost: one API call, about 0.4s.

tools.name: qase_attachment_upload
tools.description: Upload files and get back the hashes other tools reference them by. Pass `file_base64` plus `filename` for one file, or `files` for several in one request; `file_path` only works when the server runs on the same machine as the file — never on the hosted connector. The hash must then be passed in an `attachments` field; uploading alone attaches nothing. This is the only tool that sends multipart/form-data, which is why qase_api cannot send files. Cost: one API call per request, dominated by size.

files.description: Several files in one request, each entry with its own filename plus file_base64 or file_path. One round trip, hashes returned in the same order. Limits and sizing are in qase_tool_help.

file_base64.description: File content, base64 encoded. The only option on a remote server.

file_path.description: Absolute path to a file on the machine running THIS server.

file_base64.description: Single-file form. File content, base64 encoded. Use this unless the server runs on the same machine as the file.

file_path.description: Single-file form. Absolute path on the machine running THIS server; a remote server cannot see it — send file_base64 instead.

file.description: Deprecated: use file_base64 or file_path. Accepts an absolute path or base64 content.

filename.description: Original filename with extension. Required for the single-file form.

tools.name: qase_case_bulk_create
tools.description: Create up to 100 test cases in one request — the batch form of qase_case_upsert, and the right tool whenever more than one case is being written. Same fields and enum handling as qase_case_upsert; creates only, update through qase_case_upsert with `id`. Cost: one API call regardless of batch size — ten cases measured 1.2s against 5.6s as ten separate calls.

description.description: Free-form description of what the case covers

preconditions.description: State the system must be in before the steps run

postconditions.description: State to restore or verify after the steps run

priority.description: Priority label or numeric ID (0=not set, 1=high, 2=medium, 3=low)

is_flaky.description: Is flaky: 0=No, 1=Yes; a boolean works too.

suite_id.description: ID of the suite that holds the case

milestone_id.description: ID of the milestone the case belongs to

steps.description: Ordered test steps; omit for a case without steps

steps_type.description: Step style: "classic" action/expected, or "gherkin" scenario text

cases.description: Test cases to create, 1 to 100 per call

action.description: Step action (classic steps). Not needed when `shared` is set.

shared.description: Hash from `qase_shared_step_upsert` to reuse here; then `action` is not needed.

shared_step_hash.description: Alias for `shared`, the spelling a case reads back.

steps.description: Nested substeps, nesting further if needed.

tools.name: qase_case_delete
tools.description: Delete a test case by project code and ID. Its execution history goes with it and this cannot be undone; consider marking it deprecated through qase_case_upsert instead. No bulk delete — one call each, each asking the user for confirmation. Cost: one API call, about 0.4s.

tools.name: qase_case_upsert
tools.description: Create or update a single test case: with `id` it updates, without it creates. Enum fields accept a label such as "high" or the project's numeric ID. Writing more than one case? Use qase_case_bulk_create — one request instead of one per case. If the project has "Test case review" enabled, writes may need a review — run qase_discover_tools with "review". Cost: one API call, about 0.6s to create, 0.4s to update.

id.description: Case ID — if provided, updates the case; if omitted, creates a new one

description.description: Free-form description of what the case covers

preconditions.description: State the system must be in before the steps run

postconditions.description: State to restore or verify after the steps run

priority.description: Priority label or numeric ID (0=not set, 1=high, 2=medium, 3=low)

is_flaky.description: Is flaky: 0=No, 1=Yes; a boolean works too.

suite_id.description: ID of the suite that holds the case

milestone_id.description: ID of the milestone the case belongs to

steps.description: Ordered test steps; omit for a case without steps

steps_type.description: Step style: "classic" action/expected, or "gherkin" scenario text

action.description: Step action (classic steps). Not needed when `shared` is set.

shared.description: Hash from `qase_shared_step_upsert` to reuse here; then `action` is not needed.

shared_step_hash.description: Alias for `shared`, the spelling a case reads back.

steps.description: Nested substeps, nesting further if needed.

tools.name: qase_ci_report
tools.description: Report a whole finished CI run in one call: creates the run, records every result, completes it. Use qase_result_record instead when the run already exists and results arrive in stages. Each result needs a numeric `case_id` and a status; batches over 200 are split for you, up to 2000. Cost: three API operations behind one call, about 0.7s for a small run.

environment_id.description: ID of the environment the build ran against

results.description: Test results to record, 1 to 2000 per call

complete.description: Complete the run after recording results (default: true)

tools.name: qase_custom_field_delete
tools.description: Delete a custom field by ID. Reach is workspace-wide: it disappears from every project, with the values entered for it, and this cannot be undone. To remove it from one project only, edit `projects_codes` with qase_custom_field_upsert. Asks the user for confirmation first. Cost: one API call, about 0.4s.

tools.name: qase_custom_field_upsert
tools.description: Create or update a custom field. On create, `entity` (case, run, defect) and `type` are required and fixed forever — the update endpoint cannot change them. Fields are workspace-wide; scope with `projects_codes` or is_enabled_for_all_projects. Read existing fields with qase_project_context or qase_get. Cost: one call to create, two to update, 0.5-0.9s.

id.description: Custom field ID — if provided, updates; if omitted, creates

entity.description: What the field is attached to. Required when creating; cannot be changed later

type.description: Field type. Required when creating; cannot be changed later

value.description: Option titles — required for selectbox, radio and multiselect

placeholder.description: Hint shown in the empty field

default_value.description: Value a new entity gets when none is entered

is_filterable.description: Whether the field can be used as a filter

is_visible.description: Whether the field is shown on the entity

is_required.description: Whether a value must be given on create

is_enabled_for_all_projects.description: Apply to every project in the workspace, instead of only those in projects_codes

projects_codes.description: Projects the field applies to. Ignored when is_enabled_for_all_projects is true

tools.name: qase_defect_delete
tools.description: Delete a defect by project code and ID; its links to results go with it and this cannot be undone. Usually resolving it through qase_defect_upsert with `id` is the right move, so the record survives. Asks the user for confirmation first. Cost: one API call, about 0.4s.

tools.name: qase_defect_upsert
tools.description: Create or update a defect: with `id` it updates, without it creates, and then `title`, `actual_result` and `severity` are required. Severity and status are labels ("blocker", "open"…), mapped for you. For a defect born from a specific test failure use qase_triage_defect; search with qql_search before filing a duplicate. Cost: one API call, about 0.5s.

id.description: Defect ID — if provided, updates; if omitted, creates

actual_result.description: What actually happened — required when creating a defect

severity.description: How bad the defect is — required when creating a defect

status.description: Set to "resolved" to resolve the defect

tools.name: qase_discover_tools
tools.description: Search the tool catalogue by what you are trying to do — "delete", "milestone", "review", "custom field" — and get back the matching tools with their descriptions. Every tool is already listed and callable; use this when you do not know which one fits, rather than re-reading the whole list. Cost: no API call, matching happens in memory, about 3ms.

query.description: Search query to find tools by name or description. Examples: "delete", "milestone", "attachment", "suite"

tools.name: qase_environment_delete
tools.description: Delete an environment by project code and ID. Runs that referenced it lose the attribution, so filtering history by that environment stops working; this cannot be undone. Asks the user for confirmation first. Cost: one API call, about 0.4s.

tools.name: qase_environment_upsert
tools.description: Create or update an environment — a named target such as staging or production that runs are attributed to. With `id` it updates, without it creates. Existing environments come back from qase_project_context. Cost: one API call, about 0.5s.

id.description: Environment ID — if provided, updates; if omitted, creates

tools.name: qase_external_issue_link
tools.description: Link or unlink test cases and runs to issues in Jira Cloud or Jira Server — the only trackers supported. A case may link several issues; a run holds one, and a new link replaces it. Read links back with qase_get. Cost: one API call for the whole set of links, about 0.5s.

entity.description: Entity to link — test case or test run

action.description: attach creates the link, detach removes it (for runs, clears the single link)

type.description: Issue tracker integration configured for the project

id.description: Test case ID (entity="case") or test run ID (entity="run")

issues.description: External issue keys, e.g. ["PROJ-1234"]. Required for cases (attach and detach) and for attaching to a run — a run accepts exactly one issue. Omit when detaching a run.

links.description: Entities to link, processed in a single API request

tools.name: qase_get
tools.description: Fetch one known record by type and ID — case, suite, run, result, plan, defect, milestone, environment, shared_step, review, custom_field and more. Use it only when you already have the ID and want that one record; for several, anything filtered, or a loop over IDs, use qql_search — one search returns the whole page. Cost: one API call, 0.3-0.5s; ten in sequence measured 5.3s against 1.2s for one qql_search.

fields.description: Optional field projection — only return these top-level fields. Pass ["*"] for all fields.

include.description: Comma-separated list of related entities to include in the response. Cases and runs already request their external issue links by default ("external_issues" / "external_issue"); pass this only to override that.

tools.name: qase_milestone_delete
tools.description: Delete a milestone by project code and ID. Runs and cases keep existing but lose the association, so release reporting built on it stops working; this cannot be undone. Asks the user for confirmation first. Cost: one API call, about 0.4s.

tools.name: qase_milestone_upsert
tools.description: Create or update a milestone — a dated marker, typically a release, that runs and cases are grouped under. With `id` it updates, without it creates. Existing milestones come back from qase_project_context. Cost: one API call, about 0.5s.

id.description: Milestone ID — if provided, updates; if omitted, creates

tools.name: qase_plan_delete
tools.description: Delete a test plan by project code and ID. Only the plan goes — its cases and the runs made from it stay — but anything launching it by ID breaks; this cannot be undone. To change its cases use qase_plan_upsert instead. Asks the user for confirmation first. Cost: one API call, about 0.4s.

tools.name: qase_plan_upsert
tools.description: Create or update a test plan — a named, reusable set of case IDs such as a smoke or regression pack. With `id` it updates, without it creates. qase_regression_run turns a plan into a run in one call. Cost: one API call, about 0.5s, growing with the number of cases.

id.description: Plan ID — if provided, updates; if omitted, creates

tools.name: qase_project_context
tools.description: Seed everything about a project in one call: details, the full suite tree, milestones, environments, custom fields and users — make it first when starting on a project. Each collection returns its first 100; check `coverage` and pass `full: true` to page. For one record by ID qase_get is cheaper; for filtered questions use qql_search. Cost: six API calls behind one, 0.5-1.3s cold, cached 5 minutes.

full.description: Page through every collection instead of the first 100 of each (default: false). Use it when `coverage` reports one truncated; see qase_tool_help for what it costs.

tools.name: qase_project_create
tools.description: Create a project. The code must be unique in the workspace, and there is no update endpoint afterwards — title, code and access cannot be changed through the API, so choose them deliberately. Read an existing project with qase_project_context. Cost: one API call, about 1.5s.

code.description: Project code — unique per workspace, 2 to 10 characters of uppercase letters, digits or underscores

access.description: Who can access the project: everyone, a team group, or nobody but the owner

group.description: Team group hash — required when access is "group"

tools.name: qase_project_delete
tools.description: Delete an entire project by code — every case, suite, run, result, defect and milestone in it, with no trash to recover from; this cannot be undone. The most destructive call in the API; confirm the code with qase_project_context first. Asks the user for confirmation and does not proceed without it. Cost: one API call, about 0.5s.

tools.name: qase_regression_run
tools.description: Build and start a test run from a suite, a plan, or an explicit list of case IDs, in one step — it resolves the cases itself. It opens a run, it does not close one: for a finished pipeline use qase_ci_report; to assemble a run by hand use qase_run_upsert. Cost: two API calls behind one, about 1s.

environment_id.description: ID of the environment the run executes against

milestone_id.description: ID of the milestone the run belongs to

plan_id.description: Create run from an existing test plan

tools.name: qase_result_delete
tools.description: Delete one result from a run, by run ID and result hash. The case and the rest of the run are untouched; pass rates shift and this cannot be undone. To discard a whole run use qase_run_delete. Asks the user for confirmation first. Cost: one API call, about 0.4s.

tools.name: qase_result_record
tools.description: Record up to 200 results into an existing run — status, duration, comment, stacktrace, attachments — in one call, not one per test. Status is a label only: passed, failed, blocked, skipped, invalid. If the run does not exist yet and the job is finished, qase_ci_report creates, records and completes in one call. Cost: one API call for the whole list, about 0.5s.

run_id.description: Run ID to record results into

results.description: Results to record, 1 to 200 per call

tools.name: qase_review_bulk_create
tools.description: Open several test case reviews in one request — the batch form of qase_review_create, for proposing more than one change. Same fields as qase_review_create; `case_id` for an edit review, omitted for a create review. The API has no endpoints for approving, merging or declining — those are UI-only; read status with qase_review_list. Cost: one API call regardless of batch size.

reviewers.description: Reviewers: AUTHOR UUIDs (see qase_get { entity: "author" }) or emails, which resolve to them. Not user IDs. The token owner authors the review and cannot review their own review. Omit to assign them later in the UI.

postconditions.description: State to restore or verify after the steps run

suite_id.description: ID of the suite that holds the case

milestone_id.description: ID of the milestone the case belongs to

steps.description: Ordered test steps; omit for a case without steps

steps_type.description: Step style: "classic" action/expected, or "gherkin" scenario text

reviews.description: Reviews to open. Validated as a whole: if any item is invalid, NOTHING is created. Once valid, each item is processed individually and reported separately.

action.description: Step action (classic steps). Not needed when `shared` is set.

shared.description: Hash from `qase_shared_step_upsert` to reuse here; then `action` is not needed.

tools.description: Open a test case review — the pull-request flow for cases. Pass `case_id` to propose changes to an existing case (send only the fields that change), or omit it to propose a new one. Several at once? Use qase_review_bulk_create. The API has no endpoints for approving, merging or declining — those are UI-only; read status with qase_review_list. Cost: one API call, about 0.5s.

tools.name: qase_review_delete
tools.description: Delete a review by ID. This removes the proposal entirely — it does not decline it, and declining is UI-only — and merged reviews cannot be deleted; the referenced case is untouched. Cannot be undone; asks the user for confirmation first. Cost: one API call, about 0.4s.

tools.name: qase_review_list
tools.description: List a project's reviews with their current state — the only way to learn what happened to a review you opened, since the API has no endpoints for approving or merging — those are UI-only. Filter by status to see what is still open. For one review by ID, qase_get is cheaper. Cost: one API call, about 0.5s.

case_id.description: Only reviews of this test case

reviewer_uuid.description: Only reviews this author UUID is a reviewer on

search.description: Substring match on the review title

IMPORTANT: changing the proposal RESETS every approval already given; updating only `reviewers` keeps them. The API has no endpoints for approving, merging or declining — those are UI-only; read status with qase_review_list. Cost: one API call, about 0.5s.

tools.name: qase_run_complete
tools.description: Mark a test run complete so it reports as finished. It is a reporting state, not a lock — results recorded afterwards still land and change its counts. If all results are in hand at once, qase_ci_report does this as its final step. Cost: one API call, about 0.4s.

tools.name: qase_run_delete
tools.description: Delete a test run by project code and ID, together with every result in it; this cannot be undone. Rarely what you want: to stop accepting results use qase_run_complete, to fix one result use qase_result_delete. Asks the user for confirmation first. Cost: one API call, about 0.4s.

tools.name: qase_run_upsert
tools.description: Create or update a test run — the container results are recorded into, so open it before qase_result_record. Scope it to a milestone, environment, plan or case list. To build one from a suite or plan use qase_regression_run; for a finished CI job use qase_ci_report, which opens, records and closes in one call. Cost: one API call, about 0.5s.

id.description: Run ID — if provided, this is an update (note: Qase API has limited run update support)

environment_id.description: ID of the environment the run executes against

milestone_id.description: ID of the milestone the run belongs to

plan_id.description: Test plan to base run on

is_autotest.description: True when the run is produced by automation rather than a person

tools.name: qase_shared_step_delete
tools.description: Delete a shared step by project code and hash. Every case referencing it loses those steps, so the reach is far wider than one record; check references first. Cannot be undone; to change content use qase_shared_step_upsert instead. Asks the user for confirmation first. Cost: one API call, about 0.4s.

tools.name: qase_shared_step_upsert
tools.description: Create or update a shared step — a block of steps written once and reused across cases. With `hash` it updates, without it creates; shared steps are identified by hash, which qase_case_upsert takes in a step's `shared` field. Updating changes every referencing case. Cost: one API call, about 0.5s.

hash.description: Shared step hash — if provided, updates; if omitted, creates

tools.name: qase_suite_delete
tools.description: Delete a test suite by project code and ID. WARNING: the cases inside, and any child suites, are deleted with it along with their history, and `delete_cases` currently has no effect. Read the tree from qase_project_context and move what matters first. Asks the user for confirmation. Cost: one API call, about 0.4s.

delete_cases.description: Has no effect today: the server sends a field this endpoint does not accept, so the cases are deleted either way. Kept so existing callers do not break.

tools.name: qase_suite_upsert
tools.description: Create or update a test suite — the folder cases live in. With `id` it updates, without it creates; nest with `parent_id`. The existing tree comes back from qase_project_context, so read it rather than guess parent IDs. Cost: one API call, about 0.5s.

id.description: Suite ID — if provided, updates; if omitted, creates

description.description: What this suite groups — shown under the suite title in the tree

preconditions.description: Setup every case in this suite assumes, inherited by its child suites

tools.name: qase_tool_help
tools.description: Read the full documentation of one tool before calling it for the first time in a session. Every description in the tool list is deliberately short — what the tool is for and what it costs — and the details that prevent a wrong first call live here: argument semantics, limits, what cannot be undone, and which tool to use instead. Pass the tool name exactly as listed. Cost: no API call, static text, about 1ms. Cheaper than one rejected call.

tool.description: The tool name, exactly as it appears in the tool list

tools.name: qase_triage_defect
tools.description: Create a defect from a test failure with the context written into it; `title`, `actual_result` and `severity` are required. The API has no way to attach runs or results to a defect — reference them in actual_result. For a defect unrelated to a failure use qase_defect_upsert. Cost: one API call, about 0.5s; file one defect per distinct cause.

actual_result.description: Observed behavior. Required by the API

description.description: Extra context beyond the observed behavior

tools.name: qql_help
tools.description: Read the QQL reference before writing a query. Pass a `topic`: overview, syntax, entities, operators, functions, examples, aggregation or enumValues. Field names differ per entity and from the write tools, and a query naming an unknown attribute is rejected — read `entities` first. Cost: no API call, about 2ms; cheaper than one rejected qql_search.

topic.description:
Which section to return (required — one section per call):
- overview: what QQL is, overall query structure, subscription requirement
- syntax: structure, ordering, custom fields, case-sensitivity, boolean and date fields
- entities: the fields available on each entity — field names are NOT uniform across entities, so read this before writing a query against an unfamiliar one
- operators: comparison, matching, set, null, and logical operators
- functions: currentUser, activeUsers, and the now/startOf*/endOf* date functions
- examples: ready-made queries for common questions
- aggregation: SELECT (COUNT/MIN/MAX/AVG/SUM/FIRST/LAST), GROUP BY, HAVING — use this to count or summarise instead of paging through rows
- enumValues: the valid values for priority, severity, and the per-entity status fields

tools.name: qql_search
tools.description: Search any entity with Qase Query Language — filtering, cross-project, sorting, aggregation — and the right way to fetch many records at once instead of looping over qase_get. Call qql_help first for syntax, fields and enum values. Use qase_get when you already know the one ID you want. Cost: one API call, 0.5-0.9s per page; ten records here cost 1.2s against 5.3s as ten qase_get calls.

query.description:
QQL query expression. Examples:
- entity = "case" and project = "DEMO" and status = "Actual"
- entity = "defect" and severity = "blocker" and status = "open"
- entity = "result" and status = "failed" and ended >= now("-7d")
- entity = "run" and milestone ~ "Sprint 12"
See QQL documentation for full syntax and examples.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 10, max: 100)

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination

instructions:
Qase is a test management platform: test cases, suites, runs, results, defects, plans, milestones, environments, and reviews, organized by project code. This server reads and writes all of it, and reports CI results directly.

Start any new project with qase_project_context: one call returns the suite tree, milestones, environments, custom fields, and users, instead of six separate list calls. For a single known record, use qase_get. For anything filtered, cross-project, or aggregated ("failed results this week", "open blockers"), use qql_search, backed by qql_help for syntax and field references per entity.

Before the first call of a tool you have not used in this session, read qase_tool_help for it: descriptions are kept short, and the argument semantics, limits and what cannot be undone live there. Reach for the batch call before the loop. One qql_search returns ten cases about four times faster than ten qase_get calls, and one qase_case_bulk_create writes ten cases about four times faster than ten qase_case_upsert calls. Every tool's description ends with what the call costs; read it before fetching or writing records one at a time.

Writing follows one pattern throughout: qase_case_upsert, qase_run_upsert, qase_suite_upsert, qase_defect_upsert all create when `id` is omitted and update when it's given, as do every other upsert tool. A case describes what to test; a result (qase_result_record) describes what happened when it ran, into an existing run. For CI, qase_ci_report collapses create-run, record-results, and complete-run into one call. qase_regression_run builds a run from a suite, plan, or explicit case list in one step. Attachments upload separately via qase_attachment_upload — its `files` argument sends up to 20 in one request — and are referenced by hash.

Test plans, milestones, environments, shared steps, projects and workspace-wide custom fields are managed here too — search qase_discover_tools with "plan", "milestone", "environment", "shared step", "project" or "custom field" if you do not know the tool's name. A project has no update endpoint, and a custom field's entity and type are fixed once it is created.

Every tool is listed from the first request — deletes, test plans, milestones, environments, shared steps, external issue links, case reviews, and project and custom-field management included. Nothing has to be activated, and the list does not change while the server runs. If you do not know which tool fits, search with qase_discover_tools rather than concluding a capability is absent.

Enum fields (priority, severity, status, type, automation) accept a label or the project's numeric ID, either works.
